skill.name: bun-development
skill.description: Modern JavaScript and TypeScript development guidance for the Bun runtime, including setup, packages, testing, bundling, and Node.js migration.
skill.summary: Build, test, bundle, and migrate JavaScript or TypeScript projects with Bun.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt-injection content or hidden data-exfiltration intent in SKILL.md. Most static hits are Markdown fences, sample Bun server handlers, environment variable examples, or documentation links. Confirmed risks are pipe-to-shell install commands and a non-default npm registry example.

remediation.issue: Remote install scripts are piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell examples with package manager installs, checksum verification, or instructions to inspect the script before execution.

remediation.issue: The Windows install example executes a remote PowerShell script through iex.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a verified installer or package manager command, and warn users before executing remote PowerShell content.

remediation.issue: A dependency example uses a non-default npm registry mirror.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the mirror example or clearly state that users should only use trusted registries with integrity controls.

content.value_statement: Bun can simplify JavaScript and TypeScript tooling, but teams need a clear workflow before migration. This skill gives practical guidance for setup, packages, testing, bundling, runtime APIs, and Node.js migration.
actual_capabilities: Guides project initialization with bun init and common application templates.
Explains dependency installation, updates, lockfile use, and bunx commands.
Shows Bun runtime patterns for TypeScript, environment variables, files, HTTP, WebSocket, and SQLite.
Covers Bun test runner basics, matchers, mocking, watch mode, coverage, and timeouts.
Documents bundling, executable builds, production options, and Node.js migration steps.
limitations: It is a written guide and does not execute or verify commands by itself.
Some install examples download remote scripts, which require independent trust checks.
The guidance may lag behind current Bun releases or platform changes.
Examples are educational and need adaptation for production security requirements.

use_cases.title: Start a Bun Frontend Project
use_cases.description: Set up a Bun-based React, Vite, or Next.js project with TypeScript defaults and faster package workflows.

use_cases.title: Prototype Bun Services
use_cases.description: Build Bun HTTP, WebSocket, SQLite, and password hashing prototypes with native runtime APIs.

use_cases.title: Plan a Node.js Migration
use_cases.description: Map scripts, package management, testing, compatibility checks, and Bun-native replacements before migration.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Bun Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a new Bun TypeScript project. Include setup steps, basic scripts, and first test commands.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Node.js Scripts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Node.js package workflow and suggest a Bun migration plan for scripts, dependencies, tests, and lockfiles.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Runtime APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Bun service design and recommend native APIs for file handling, HTTP routing, WebSockets, SQLite, and password hashing.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Production Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Bun build checklist covering bundling, executable targets, source maps, environment files, and deployment risks.

output_examples.input: I need a Bun starter project for a TypeScript API.
output_examples.output: Project setup steps with recommended scripts, dependency commands, runtime choices, and a first test plan.

output_examples.input: I want to migrate a Node.js service to Bun.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering scripts, package manager replacement, compatibility issues, Bun-native APIs, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: I need to bundle a Bun CLI for production.
output_examples.output: A build plan with target selection, minification, source maps, executable output, and asset handling notes.

best_practices: Verify remote installation scripts before running them, especially pipe-to-shell commands.
Pin package versions and use trusted registries for reproducible dependency installs.
Run Bun tests and build checks after changing runtime, bundler, or migration settings.
anti_patterns: Piping remote scripts directly into a shell without inspection or checksum verification.
Switching npm registries globally without confirming trust, availability, and package integrity.
Assuming every Node.js API behaves identically under Bun without testing edge cases.

faq.question: Does this skill install Bun automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command examples and guidance. Users decide which commands to run.

faq.question: Does it support both JavaScript and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on Bun workflows for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, tests, and bundling.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from Node.js?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers script replacement, package manager changes, compatibility checks, and Bun-specific alternatives.

faq.question: Does it cover server development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Bun.serve HTTP handlers, WebSocket examples, SQLite usage, and password hashing patterns.

faq.question: Are the install commands risk-free?
faq.answer: No. Remote install scripts and registry changes require trust checks before execution.

faq.question: Can it replace official Bun documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use official docs for version-specific behavior and release changes.
